TaroCard.DirectReading: This is the time for new beginnings. Follow your heart and take some risks. Put yourself out there and be willing to try something new. You may be offered a new opportunity or invitation to an important invent. A new relationship may suddenly appear in your life. The best approach to take is one with spontaneity and an adventurous spirit. In Love Tarot, there could be delusions about the perfect relationship. It’s time to review how your perceive relationships. Take a risk, but don’t be careless.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: Be careful not to commit to something you are unsure about. This is not the time to take too many risks. Being impulsive or reckless can have negative consequences. You may experience a period of feeling overwhelmed. You need to take the necessary time to gain a deeper understanding of your situation. Your lack of clarity or foresight is hindering your decision making abilities. In Love Tarot, there could be the start of a new relationship.
TaroCard.Meaning: Ruled by Uranus, the powerful and unpredictable Roman sky god. This portrays a young traveler embarking on life's journey. The bag on his shoulder holds the tools of life, and the white rose denotes pure intentions. Indicates a willingness to leap into the unknown and start anew.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is the time to focus your energy and apply yourself. Know that you have all the skills necessary to overcome the obstacles that come your way. Be adaptable and get creative. This is also a great time to market yourself. Direct your energy towards achieving your goals and success is sure to come. The Magician Tarot card urges you to get into action and put your talents to use. The magician can represent a male lover or devotee. Be careful you don’t want to change your lover through manipulation.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may be experiencing a creative block or lack of direction. It’s important to observe your surroundings and become willing to face your problems. You may feel a lack of self-confidence or indecision about a certain situation. It’s important to remember to use your skills to navigate through difficulties.
TaroCard.Meaning: Ruled by Mercury, the messenger of the gods. A strong man lifts a wand, while the tools of magical practice are set before him. Signifies the channeling of life force from above to below. This deeply masculine card suggests powerful energy. The Magician has the ability to summon new ideas.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is the time to trust your feelings. There is more going on beneath the surface. The High Priestess appears when you need to listen to your inner voice. This is not a time to act quickly. Rather, there is something more you need to learn about the situation. You may find yourself triggered or agitated as something is stirring in your unconscious. Meditation and contemplation will bring you the answers that you seek. In Love Tarot, you may feel an inner connection to your mate. Some hidden information needs to come to light. The High Priestess can represent a female lover or devotee.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may be ignoring your inner voice and not listening to your gut feelings. This is not the time to over-intellectualize as this could hamper your problem solving abilities. Your unconscious may be trying to convey something to you that you are unwilling to hear. Observe your surroundings. More knowledge is required and do not make any rash decisions at this time.
TaroCard.Meaning: Ruled by the Moon. With the mark of Isis on her forehead and crucifix around her neck - symbols of spirituality - she is balanced between the pillars of peace and severity. Signifies a mystical quietness.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is a great time to get creative. Your creative energies will result in abundance and self-realization. Your hard work will pay off both spiritually and materially. You will be able to anticipate spiritual and material abundance through the efforts of your labor. The Empress often indicates fertility, childbirth and marriage. Your home life is important to you and it’s important to fill it with things that bring your peace and harmony. This is also the time to tap into your feminine power. In Love Tarot, the Empress can represent a relationship full of possibility. This is fertile ground for a new relationship to emerge. The Empress can represent the exchange of love, commitment and marriage.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may experience a period of financial uncertainty. Work can feel laborious and mundane. Financial matters can be tested and you may find that you are struggling to make ends meet. Spiritually, the Empress reversed can indicate that you are being too greedy with your emotions or you may be holding on to your money too tightly. A lack of creativity is hindering your growth.
TaroCard.Meaning: Ruled by Venus, the Roman goddess of love. Symbolizes the power of motherhood, the earth, and practical wisdom. With a garland of stars and images of fruits, the Empress is both beautiful and bountiful. The stars in her crown represent the signs of the Zodiac, indicating that she is the mother of all.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is the time to gain control of your surroundings. Use your intellect to overcome your obstacles and challenges. The projects you have embarked on have solid foundations and will prove to be successful. You are respected in your community and others may come to you for advice. Your drive for success needs to be appropriately focused. You may get a job promotion based on your ability to put things in order. You may be recognized for your leadership abilities. In Love Tarot, the Emperor can represent a structured and organized partnership. In this case, you can expect to feel secure and protected by your partner
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may need to take more responsibility in a particular situation. Your reluctance to grow up is hindering your personal relationships. You may feel as though you want to run away from your problems. Potentially, there could be a situation that affects your self-confidence. You may be over thinking things. Generally the Emperor reversed indicates that projects will be halted. Progress may be difficult at this time. You also need to be careful that you are not being too forceful with those at work or at home.
TaroCard.Meaning: Associated with the sign of Aries, the ram, the Emperor represents the earthly father. Depicted as the enthroned Roman emperor, he is the personification of temporal power. Suggests the accumulation of material wealth. Although disciplined and visionary, he keeps his emotions under wraps.

TaroCard.DirectReading: There may be situations that come up that cause you to struggle with questions of major significance. You may be forced to examine your own values and belief systems. The Hierophant encourages you to find freedom through knowledge and exploration. He may indicate that it is a good time for you to seek counsel from someone who is more experienced. There may also be an invitation to a wedding or religious ceremony. In Love Tarot, there may be a need for spiritual guidance within your relationship. This is a relationship based on traditions and values.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: There may have been a misrepresentation of the truth. You may be getting bad advice and you, or someone else, may be withholding information to gain authority. The reversed Hierophant warns you that your thinking is too fixated. Your own stubbornness is preventing your personal growth and may be causing friction in your relationships. There may be areas in your life that require some adjustments. Your ideas may need to be more original and creative.
TaroCard.Meaning: Associated with the sign of Taurus, the bull. With a scepter in one hand and the other raised in blessing, he symbolizes the pope, the spiritual father, and the trinity - mind, body, spirit. The card offers mercy and compassion and indicates a need for approval and conformity.

TaroCard.DirectReading: You are at an important crossroad and you may have to make an important decision. This choice often will yield two very different results, so you must carefully examine the repercussions of each choice. You may find yourself being tested before you transition into a new phase of life. A new relationship may enter your life. This relationship will have a soul connection. You may have to choose between two potential mates.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: There could be misunderstandings between you and those you care about. You must be willing to take responsibility for the choices that you have made. This may be a good time to explore whether your relationships are healthy. You or your partner may be experiencing a fear of commitment.
TaroCard.Meaning: Associated with the sign of Gemini, the twins. The image depicts lovers in an embrace, while an angel looks on. Gemini seeks a soul mate, a new love. This card suggests love, friendship, and partnership. Also represents the duality of earthly and divine love.

TaroCard.DirectReading: You have all the tools necessary to triumph over any obstacles that stand in your way. This is a period of action, change and new experiences. Your self-control and will power will aid you in victory. The more effort you put out, the more successful you will become. Self-discipline is necessary. This is a time to remain focused and stay devoted to managing your conflicting thoughts and feelings. In Love Tarot, each member of the partnership must work on their own level of individuation. It’s important to maintain a sense of yourself while in this relationship. Clear communication of personal needs should be addressed. This relationship has the potential to flourish if the energies are directed appropriately.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may feel out of control or overwhelmed. Your energy is not being directed appropriately. You have lost sight of your goals. Your lack of focus has caused you to feel anxious and frazzled. You may feel torn between two directions. Your conflicting feelings are causing you to lose energy and feel pressure. This is the time to take a step back and regain your perspective and sense of clarity.
TaroCard.Meaning: Linked to cancer and the Moon. Twin sphinxes - one black, one white - draw a chariot emblazoned with the symbol of yig and yang. Balance negative and positive forces to achieve success. Maintain focus and attend to details.

TaroCard.DirectReading: You can reach your goals by examining the areas in your life that bring you strength. Your may find yourself in a situation that requires courage and fearlessness. A new opportunity will require some risk taking. Self-discipline is your greatest ally. As you gain control over your inner desires and impulses, you now find that you can stand up to those that are pushing you around. The best approach to dealing with conflicts is through neutrality and diplomacy. In Love Tarot, there needs to be a gentler approach to your partner. You cannot force someone to change. Physical touch can be healing.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may feel as though you do not have the strength to confront a situation. A lack of self-confidence may be influencing your judgment. You need to assert yourself to regain your sense of courage and inner strength. It’s important not to lose your nerve in the face of a new opportunity. You may be giving in to your inner impulses. The reversed Strength card indicates an over-emphasis on security. Staying in your comfort zone can cause you to miss out on new experiences.
TaroCard.Meaning: Linked to the sign of Leo. The lion is a sexual animal, but his base instincts are checked by the caress of a maiden. Message: Use your head and not your heart. Exercise restraint; hold your power in reserve.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is a period that requires meditation and contemplation. You must go within and do some soul searching to truly discover who you are. Your answers will come from within your own, inner self. You may need to take things more slowly as you decide which path or strategy is the right one for you. This is a journey that requires solitude and faith. Before proceeding into action, you must thoroughly consider your plans for self-discovery and your desired goals for personal growth. A wise teacher may offer you important advice. In Love Tarot, it’s important to be careful that you make time for yourself. Each partner must not lose sight of their own personal journey.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You have not been paying attention to your inner self. The reversed Hermit is a reminder that you need to slow down and take some time for yourself. In some cases, you may feel isolated and lonely. It’s important to remember to connect with those you care about. Your own fear may be inhibiting your personal growth and willingness to go within. Be careful of becoming so consumed with doing things your way that you have passed up good advice from a wise counsel.
TaroCard.Meaning: Associated with the sign of Virgo, the natural healer of the Zodiac. An old man leaning on a staff holds up a shining lantern. He shows the way to wisdom and enlightenment. This strong healing card suggests looking inward, seeking the inner path; an opportunity for selfknowledge.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is a period of rapid change and new opportunity. It’s important to remember that everything comes in cycles and stages. You are beginning a new life cycle, one that promises fortunate circumstances. Things have been set in motion that you have little control of, yet if you accept the process, change and growth will occur. This is a process of destiny and if you let it work through you, events of great significance can manifest.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may feel as though you have no control over your current circumstances. There could be setbacks or delays in your endeavors. You good luck has wavered and you must wait until the wheel has made a full circle. The path you on may not provide the results you want. Things may have to get worse before they can get better.
TaroCard.Meaning: Ruled by Jupiter, the planet of expansion. This card can indicate a turn for the better or receiving one's just reward for past deeds. Fortune, power, movement, and change are all here. The wheel turns, revealing the cyclical nature of life.

TaroCard.DirectReading: You may need to evaluate your present course of action. This is the time to take a moment to pause and re-examine the directions you are taking. You may have to restructure your life according to what you feel is right and just. In some cases, the Justice card is a reminder that you need become accountable for your choices. There is a need for truth and balance. The Justice card can indicate the onset of legal issues. Things should proceed with fairness and integrity. The outcome should be in your favor. In Love Tarot, a balance is needed within oneself and one’s relationship. This is the time to re-evaluate your relationship. Be open and levelheaded.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may be forced to make a decision that you have been reluctant to confront. It’s important to remember to be honest with yourself. There may be a situation in which you will not be treated fairly. In some cases, there could be a setback in you getting what you feel you deserve. You may be too focused on your position and status in society. Justice reversed always represents an imbalance of some kind. You need to find equilibrium between your conscience and inner desires.
TaroCard.Meaning: Associated with the sign of Libra, the scales. Justice holds a sword in one hand and the scales in the other. Decisions will be made - fairly. Suggests a possible court appearance. Can relate to wills or divorce.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Hanged Man signifies the awakening of a new consciousness. You may have to re-examine your priorities and determine if they conform to the spiritual principals that you wish to live by. Sometimes The Hanged Man indicates that an important life lesson needs to be understood and accepted. During this period you may feel tested by outside influences. You may be forced to sacrifice something you feel attached to. The Hanged Man urges you to let go and relinquish your perception of control. In Love Tarot, you may have to let go of old ideas. Sacrifices must be made in order for the relationship to move forward. There could be conflict within the relationship. The relationship is not on solid ground.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may be choosing to live in a fantasy or you are failing to be true to yourself. Perhaps you are sacrificing too much of yourself in order to keep the people closest to you happy. You may be lingering in the past or you are too consumed with controlling the outcomes of your decisions. Your lack of faith is preventing you from making necessary changes in your life. The best approach would be to surrender and go with the flow.
TaroCard.Meaning: Calm and alert, the Hanged Man doesn't appear uncomfortable in his suspended state. Suggests a step backward, a distancing from everyday concerns. Indicates a period of rest and reassessment.

TaroCard.DirectReading: You are in the process of a personal transformation. A life cycle has ended and another is beginning. There may be a phase in your life that is coming to an end. Examples of this could include a child leaving the home, the end of a relationship, a graduation, or the death of someone you may know. The Death card indicates that there is going to be a major change in your life. It will be an experience that leads to an important transformation. You may find that your life takes a new and unexpected turn. In Love Tarot, you can expect a transformative period within the relationship. This is the time for new beginnings. Old patterns and communication methods may have become outdated.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may be unwilling to change or are preventing important transitions the need to occur within your life. You may be in denial regarding the conclusion of a life stage, relationship or important event that needs to happen if you are to move forward in your life. You may feel a reluctance to look forward due to your attachment to the past. You may be forced to give up what you do not necessarily want to. Resisting change makes the process of letting go much more painful.
TaroCard.Meaning: A skeletal rider on a pale horse bears the banner of a white rose. This card usually indicates rebirth or transition rather than physical death. Accept change so that rebirth can occur.

TaroCard.DirectReading: Balance and moderation are now in need. You need to take the time to step back and re-evaluate what isn’t working in your life. The Temperance card suggests that all things need to be handled with moderation and tolerance. This is a good time to explore what feels as though it is on the verge of becoming out of control. In some cases, the Temperance card can indicate a new relationship or a situation in which you and someone else must come together to get a task done. In Love Tarot, there is harmony within your relationship. The best approach is utilizing balance and patience to move your relationship forward. This is a period of self-realization for both you and your partner.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: Your behavior may be too reckless or extreme. You may be overreacting to a situation. It’s important to remember to handle things with neutrality and moderation. You need to be careful that your ambitions don’t cause you to make radical decisions. It would be wise to consider a compromise. You may feel as though your life is not in balance. It’s important to take a step back and make time for yourself.
TaroCard.Meaning: Linked with the sign of Sagittarius, the archer. An angel pours liquid from one vessel into another, blending the essences. This card represents a mixing of elements within oneself and within relationships. This auspicious card brings good health.

TaroCard.DirectReading: You may feel trapped and unable to control the outcome of a situation. You may feel imprisoned by your own ambitions and motivations. In some cases, the Devil card reminds us that we are too attached to material possessions, unhealthy relationships, substances or our financial position. The Devil encourages you to resist the power of your primitive nature. You also need to be aware of how you are treating others. This is the time to become aware of behaviors that may be selfish. One solution is to start thinking about how you can help others. In relationship readings, the Devil suggests that you may need to take a good look at your relationships. Your attachments to others may be harmful or unhealthy. There could be issues with co-dependency and enmeshment. Negative patterns and behaviors are causing an unhealthy relationship.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may experience a new sense of freedom. You may have or are now willing to free yourself from the restraints that you have imposed upon yourself. You are no longer controlled by your darker impulses. Your ties to issues of materialism or to your relationships no longer hold you prisoner. In some cases, the Devil reversed can indicate liberation and freedom from old ideas and perceptions. However, if you are still unwilling to deal with your attachments, the Devil reversed can have further negative interpretations. In this case, there may be an over-attachment to material possessions. This refers to greed and the need to control others.
TaroCard.Meaning: Associated with Capricorn, the goat. A tethered couple looks away in misery under the Devil's yoke. Represents emotional, spiritual, physical bondage; facial attachments or relationships based on material gain. These chains can be broken with willpower. Can also relate to deviant sexual tendencies or cults.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This may be a period in which you experience sudden change or upheaval. The Tower can indicate a move, change of job, or shift in an important relationship. Now is the time to set yourself free from situations that have been holding you back. Your belief system may no longer be working for you. If this is the case, you must be willing to let go of your old ideas. You may have to let go of ineffective behavior patterns and realign yourself with what you truly value. Expect a period of chaos and uncertainty as you transition into a new way of being. In Love Tarot, external forces are affecting your relationship. It’s time to express who you really are. It’s important to get to your own truth. Old masks and personas no longer will imprison you.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a positive respect, the Tower reversed informs you that you are in the process of liberating yourself. Disruption and chaos are coming to an end. You have a new found sense of clarity and acceptance. In some cases, however, the Tower reversed can indicate some form of injustice in your life. You may feel trapped in a situation that you wish to be freed from, but do not know how to proceed. You may be required to confront a situation that you could have avoided.
TaroCard.Meaning: Ruled by Mars, the Roman god of war. Lightning strikes the Tower, and its golden crown crashes earthward. Outmoded structures are smashed cleanly, leaving the way open to complete change. The Tower is a card of radical transformation.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Star is a card of prosperity and spiritual growth. This will be a period of healing and regeneration. Take the time to balance and center yourself. Trust your inner wisdom and intuition as it will bring you comfort and relief. You have a new sense of hope and have the confidence to proceed in your endeavors. You may also discover a new sense of inspiration and creativity. The Star encourages you to apply yourself as you will be rewarded for your efforts. In Love Tarot, there is harmony within you relationship. You can expect a deep appreciation for one another. The Star can indicate the deepening of one’s relationship through spirituality.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may feel as though there is a lack of hope. It’s important to stay aware of the beauty that surrounds you. A lack in self-confidence and low self-esteem can be prohibiting you from feeling happy. There may be feelings of anxiety and fear. This is the time to find faith in yourself and in the Divine. Try to focus on the things that you do have. In a tarot reading, the Star reversed also warns of rigid and stubborn thinking. The best action to take would be that of letting go. Surrender to the process and let your inner wisdom guide you.
TaroCard.Meaning: Coupled with the sign of Aquarius. Just as the young woman pours water, Aquarius pours forth creativity and new ideas. This card denotes hope and inspiration, perhaps from an unexpected source. The foundation is sound; change is natural and balanced. A bright future is in store.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is the time to take pause and remain open. You may experience a flood of deep emotions as you struggle with some form of internal conflict. You must be willing to face your unconscious instincts and behaviors. Important information needs to rise to the surface. Be willing to reflect upon your past behaviors. The Moon also indicates the need to pay attention to your dreams, feelings and intuition. This is a good time to trust your “gut” feelings. In Love Tarot, you can gain new intuitive information about your relationship. Trust your gut. The Moon indicates the desire for a soul mate. There may be conflict below the surface.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: Your own illusions are prohibiting you from seeing the truth. There may be some deception surrounding you. This is the time to rely on your spiritual connection. New perspectives and clarity will ultimately emerge. Try not to make any major decisions right now. It would be best to wait until you see the truth of the situation.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Moon rules the subconscious. Psychic powers are revealed; intuition is strong. As the Moon waxes and wanes, beware of deception and the shifting sand of superficial relationships. Also suggests that unusual, supernatural events may occur.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is a period of success and achievement. Projects or endeavors will reach completion. This is a great time for celebration. Time spent with family and friends will be emotionally gratifying. You will feel healthy and free and may experience a change of perspective. Expect news that is positive; such as births, financial successes, marriages, stability or the completion of projects. The Sun indicates an overall happiness and feelings well-being. In Love Tarot, you can expect joy and happiness within your relationship. This is a period of mutual attraction, fulfillment and happiness.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: Success will be accomplished; however, the process may be delayed. Happiness can be attained, but there will be some limitations. Not all that you expected will materialize. In some cases, your expectations may be unrealistic. This would be a good time to review your perceptions of your situations. You may experience low energy and mild depression. In terms of relationships, the Sun reversed can indicate quarrels and miscommunication. You may feel unloved or not appreciated.
TaroCard.Meaning: A cherub rides a white pony through a field of sunflowers under a benevolent sun. Solar energy is powerful and fulfilling, bringing growth, contentment, and positive energy. Happy relationships and satisfying creative endeavors follow. Could be the time to expand your horizons, professionally or socially.

TaroCard.DirectReading: Judgment represents the end of another cycle or life stage. This is the time to ask yourself if the current direction of your life is aligned with you highest good. Judgment often calls for self-evaluation and self-exploration. You need to review the course of your actions and determine if you need to correct any past mistakes. The Judgment card can also represent the need to make an essential life decision. In this case, it is extremely important to evaluate the possible consequences of your decision. Know that your decision can be transformational. In Love Tarot, your relationship may need to take a new direction. It’s time to review your relationship through a new perspective. Self-evaluation is required. You may experience a spiritual renewal in your relationship.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: The reversed Judgment card can indicate unhappiness, isolation or difficulties with overcoming your obstacles. You may have to deal with the consequences of the decisions you made in the past. This is the time to take constructive measures. You may also find that you are fearful about making important decisions. You cannot prevent change from happening. If you are unwilling to accept changes, you will be unable to grow. Unwanted changes could make you feel out of control and helpless.
TaroCard.Meaning: Ruled by Pluto, the god of the underworld. An angel sounds a trumpet, suggestive of the final judgment. This is card of transformation. A fresh start is possible. It is time to forgive and forget, or perhaps do some soul-searching.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The World indicates wholeness, both spiritually and individually. You are coming to an end of an important life cycle or stage. You can expect the completion of a project, relationship or important situation. Everything is as it should be and the achievement of goals will be met with success. Your hard work will reap rewards. You have achieved a sense of balance within yourself and feel whole and complete. As you complete this last stage, plan to begin something new. This is a great time to explore new areas of interest. In Love Tarot, the World card represents the completion of a relationship. The lessons have been learned. This is a creative and harmonious relationship based on the personal development of both partners. In some cases, the World can indicate a mutual and harmonious separation.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: There could be delays or setbacks in achieving your goals. You may not be willing to accept change or your fears are preventing you from completing important tasks or projects. You may be apt to quit a situation rather than see it through. A lack of commitment may be preventing you from achieving your goals.
TaroCard.Meaning: A robed figure commands the elements and forces of the universe. This card represents the completion of life's circle and mystical unity with the cosmos. The power of transcendence is within reach.

TaroCard.DirectReading: An upright Ace of Wands can indicate a new venture or enterprise. Use your energy to open new doors. With sexual energy high you can look for a new romantic relationship or new found attraction in a current partnership. Wands can also refer to fertility, pregnancy and birth. It is the time to manifest your dreams, with power and optimism as your driving force. Trust yourself, explore new ideas, life paths, and relationships.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the Ace of Wands can indicate indecision, lack of direction, or a need for commitment. You may feel discouraged, frustrated or helpless in achieving your goals. Now is the time to reevaluate your intentions and your current path. In love Tarot, your partnership may struggle with a lack of commitment. There could be potential infidelity within your relationship. A reversed Ace of Wands can refer to stubborn and pessimistic people; examine your motivations and interactions in this regard.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Ace of Wands is associated with creative enterprises and new ideas. It denotes power, fertility, new beginnings and energy. When the Ace of Wands comes up in a Tarot reading, you can expect new opportunities. A new relationship may enter your life. You may experience a change in feelings that will influence your life direction or sense of purpose.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Two of Wands indicates the need to step back and let things unfold. Your leadership abilities have set things in motion. Your creative ideas and endeavors will prove to be successful. Plan, be patient, and use your energy to be creative. Your hard work will pay off. Travel may soon be required for business, even possibly relocation.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the Two of Wands can indicate feelings of frustration and anxiety as you are waiting for something to develop. You may question your choices, feel unfocused, or have a loss of interest in attaining certain goals. Projects can face delays, obstacles or bad negotiations. Carefully consider any new partnerships. Examine your own self-doubt, as well as any pride issues that can inhibit your growth.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Two of Wands is the card of potential. This is a period of waiting. You have completed the first stage of a project or endeavor. Now you must have faith in its future.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Three of Wands encourages you to collaborate with others. Your ability to form solid foundations has earned you respect by your colleagues. Your projects and investments will thrive and expand. You may receive a new job offer. In love Tarot, the Three of Wands often indicates a new phase of a relationship. Spiritually you can achieve growth through meditation and contemplation.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the Tarot card meanings of the Three of Wands refer to issues of unrealistic expectations or delays in projects. Your collaborations with others may be inhibiting the growth of a project or endeavor. The objective at hand may not be successful due to unrealistic expectations, delays or a lack of initiative. However, do not lose faith because the reversed Three of Wands can indicate a necessary delay or waiting period. A patient and practical approach may help your project get back on track again
TaroCard.Meaning: The Three of Wands typically indicates the initial completion of a task or project. The project you have been working on is on the verge of success. You have, at last, established strong foundations and you are about to achieve your goals is in the near future. However, there is still more to be done. This is the time to continue forward.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Four of Wands depicts happiness and contentment. Celebrate your accomplishments and the rewards that follow. In some cases, the Four of Wands can indicate the purchase of a new home. Your property and investment matters flourish. In love Tarot, commitments are strong and there is happiness and security. If you are single, look for marriage or engagement. Your success will enable you to embark on new journeys; take a vacation or holiday, and enjoy your life!
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the Four of Wands often indicates feelings of insecurity and disappointment. The good news though is that these obstacles are only temporary and success will come in due time. For now though, it is best to hunker down and get back to work. By keeping your goals in sight and not getting discouraged, you should succeed in the long run.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Four of Wands often is a card of celebration and rites of passages. It typically represents periods of stability and prosperity. This is a direct result of your energy, passion and dedication in achieving your goals.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Five of Wands indicates that this is the time to prove yourself. Cast your doubts aside and go for what you want. You will find new clarity and energy if you explore your inner feelings and emotions. Your energy can be focused in physical activity, particularly group sports. This may be a period in which your relationships struggle. Remain flexible and keep the lines of communication open.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: Typically, a reversed Five of Wands indicates a coming evolution of inner peace and harmony where your struggles are replaced with feelings of well-being. Although you may have found resolutions for your current circumstances, you may still need to work through feelings of self-doubt and perhaps a lack of confidence. Evaluate your current situation to see if you are spread too thin. You may need to prioritize your energy in order to find fulfillment.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Five of Wands denotes forceful action, competition and facing your challenges. This card urges you participate with assertiveness. This is time to rise to the occasion and approach your opposition with energy and determination.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is a time to celebrate your triumphs and personal achievements! The Six of Wands indicates good news and favorable circumstances, maybe even a new job. Use your confidence to be victorious in the outcome of your goals. The Six of Wands is the card of acknowledgment. In love Tarot, your relationships are in a place of understanding. If you are single, you may meet the person who recognizes your uniqueness.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: A reversed Six of Wands often refers to delays. You may lack the energy and self-confidence to follow through on important financial and business matters. In some circumstances, you may be confronted with disagreements, conflicts or miscommunications. Your lack of self-confidence is inhibiting your success. In love Tarot, your relationship may be confronted with new issues that test your levels of commitment. There is also a concern regarding feelings of being undervalued by your partner.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Six of Wands is the card of victory and achievement. Your ambition and hard work will, at last, be rewarded. You can expect improvements in all areas of your life.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Seven of Wands reminds you to take a stand for what you believe in. In a situation coming to a head, you have the advantage. Your determination will prove to help you in the end. Triumph is yours if stay true to yourself and your causes. This may be a period when tempers rise. It would be wise to stay collected and not lose your cool. This is great time to seek new employment as your skills will outshine your competition. In troubled relationships, seek to open channels of communication. If your relationship is being challenged by a fellow rival, now is the time to fight for your partner.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: When the Seven of Wands appears in a reversed position, it can indicate that you are not up to the challenges in your life and may be inclined to run away from your problems. Your fear of the future may inhibit your personal progress and growth. Be careful not to miss new opportunities. You may lack confidence and courage; so find your inner strength. In a negative sense, you may be fighting a losing battle that you may be better off just walking away from.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Seven of Wands is the card of independent action. It often refers to creative pursuits and learning. Regardless of one’s challenges, the Seven of Wands proves that you can overcome your obstacles through diligence and tenacity. Standing your ground will enable you to triumph over competition and rivalry.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Eight of Wands is a card of manifestation. Things are now working in your favor. You can expect rapid movement and change. This is also a great time for self-promotion or the marketing of one’s self. Look for new projects, or to travel, or to move forward in your career. Be certain to focus on each task one at a time. The Eight of Wands requires concentration and navigation. In love, be ready for a passionate relationship.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the Eight of Wands indicates wasted energy and impulsive behavior. You need to slow down, think before you act, and observe your surroundings. The energy of the Eight of Wands can produce fear and anxiety which may make you vulnerable to impulsive decisions or actions. Take the time to review your direction. Sometimes it is best to do nothing. Do not act impulsively in a love relationship or there could be negative consequences.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Eight of Wands is a card of energy, action and movement. When the Eight of Wands appears in a Tarot reading, it signifies that timing is in your favor. Things that have been stagnant or inactive will suddenly have new energy. This is particularly true for business matters and romantic relationships. If you have found yourself struggling with issues that you did not know how to manage, the Eight of Wands often indicate new clarity and broader perspectives.

TaroCard.DirectReading: You are facing your final test before achieving victory. The Nine of Wands indicates you will need to stay strong, overcome current obstacles, and defend your position. You have the advantage if you remain vigilant and cautious. The Nine of wands can indicate that past suffering may be causing fear and trepidation. For the sake of your relationships and spiritual journey, you must be willing to work through your fears and trepidations.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the Nine of Wands can indicate that you are not speaking up for yourself or that you are not appropriately defending yourself. You may be experiencing feelings of being overwhelmed. Your lack of self-confidence is inhibiting you from standing behind your convictions. Your fears may be causing you to not believe in yourself. You may be in a situation in which you did not accurately perceive the strength of your opponent. In some cases, someone may have caught you off guard or is deceiving you.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Nine of Wands urges you to stand your ground. This is the time to find your inner strength and courage. Although you may feel overwhelmed, you will achieve your goals if you remain determined and resilient.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Ten of Wands can indicate that you are seriously on overload. You may have taken on too much and need to delegate. Use your diligence to complete an important, but stressful project at work. Take time for yourself by setting boundaries between work and personal life. The Ten of Wands can indicate health issues, particularly body aches and pains.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a positive respect, the reversed Ten of Wands indicates you will feel relief from pressures and obligations. Feelings of stress and worry begin to lift. There is an improvement in your health. You are now free to take some time for yourself. Negatively you may feel a lack of trust in people and increased tension and strain. Alienation will come from too much focus on your goals.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Ten of Wands indicates feelings of stress, pressure and being overwhelmed. This is a period in which your responsibilities are taking a toll on you.

TaroCard.DirectReading: When the Page of Wands appears in a Tarot reading, he can represent an invitation or news of a new adventure. You may change jobs, continue your education, or start another sort of endeavor. This will be a time in which your ideas and plans come into fruition. In love Tarot, the Page of Wands can indicate a fiery new relationship. Enjoy, but remember, the Page of Wands’ exploratory nature keeps him moving and he may lose interest quickly.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: With the Page of Wands in a reversed position it is important not to be impulsive in your decisions. You may lack energy, focus and feel scattered. You may be treated unfairly by someone you know. Be wary with whom you place your trust. The Page of Wands reversed can refer to an unsatisfying career or unemployment. In love Tarot, a lack commitment may lead to a broken heart.
TaroCard.Meaning: Adorned with a medallion of the sun, the Page is shouting out a message. Good news is on the way. The Page of Wands is the ultimate adventurer. He is passionate and energetic. He has a love for excitement and faces his challenges with bravery and enthusiasm. The Page of Wands is always ready for something new.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Knight of Wands is all about movement, energy and action, and often signifies change of great magnitude. In some cases, it can indicate a move, travel or an important new venture. The Knight of Wands represents the fire within us and the energy that drives us. You could have news of an important project. Remember that your confidence is your strongest selling point. In love, the Knight of Wands can indicate a passionate relationship.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: The Knight of Wands in reverse can indicate that you are being hasty or are not following through on your intentions. Your job may seem unstable or your projects may not have solid foundations. You may be experiencing a series of changes in your life that are causing you to lose synergy and balance. It’s important to keep an eye on your own behavior. You may have a tendency to try to force yourself on others or those who are unreliable. A partner may not be willing to commit. The Knight of Wands may also indicate separation due to a move or travel.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Knight bears the emblem of the dragon - fiery, passionate, and ready to take on the world. This is the sign of the explorer. Also signifies travel, adventure; a change of residence.

TaroCard.DirectReading: A successful balance of ambition, energy and communication is associated with the Queen of Wands. It may indicate that a well balanced, mature woman will offer you some important advice. Your career abilities are well recognized; seize this time for action. In love Tarot, you may come across a passionate new love interest. A new level of equality and balance will be experienced with your partner.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the Queen of Wands often refers to narrow-mindedness and too much emphasis on one’s ambitions. It may indicate a domineering and manipulative woman who is alienated from others. Be careful not to hide your insecurity in rigidity and self-righteousness. In love Tarot, the reversed Queen of Wands can indicate a woman trying to interfere with your relationship. Your level of self-sufficiency could prevent closeness with a partner or within a relationship.
TaroCard.Meaning: This lovely Queen has charms to soothe the savage beasts - witness the cat snoozing on her lap. The Sunshine Lady brings light and love to the people around her. The Queen of Wands represents the emotionally mature female. She has the remarkable ability to balance her heart and mind.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The King of Wands can indicate sound advice from a fatherly figure; a mature, generous and passionate man. In your career, you stand on your own, supported by your creativity, motivation and strong communication skills. You may receive support from a male employer or team leader. You will be rewarded for your labors. In love Tarot, you will find energy, generosity and strength in a partner. Loyalty and passion go hand in hand.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the King of Wands refers to a man who is intolerant, impatient and self-righteous. This may indicate an authority figure whose behavior is egotistical and obstinate. You may be forced to take a stand for what you believe in. Beware of get-rich quick schemes. Be certain that you are not the one exhibiting behaviors that are insensitive to others.
TaroCard.Meaning: The King of Wands is depicted with the lion rampant at his back. He has the strength to back up his ideas and vision. This self-starter can rarely sit still. Honest and dependable; a natural leader and a man of action.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is a period of new beginnings, particularly with your relationships. The Ace of Cups may indicate an engagement, marriage or pregnancy. You may also experience an abundance of creative energy or ideas. Expect abundance in all areas of your life. Investments and projects will prosper. No matter which career path you choose, success is sure to follow.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the Ace of Cups can indicate the loss or separation of a significant relationship. However, this is not always the case. On an emotional level, you may feel discord or disappointment with your partner or friendships. A relationship may lack the commitment that you desire. This may be a period in which you must deal with your emotions. In some cases, the Ace of Cups reversed can refer to past trauma or grief that needs to be dealt with.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Ace of Cups is the card of emotional rebirth. It represents the spiritual aspects of love and commitment. Its tarot card meanings often refer to love, joy, happiness, and feelings of well-being.

TaroCard.DirectReading: Love and partnerships are in the air. The Two of Cups can refer to marriage, proposals, or the start of a new romantic relationship. If there has been a conflict with someone you care about, you can expect a resolution. Cooperation and negotiation may be needed. Working as a team may further your endeavors. In some cases, the Two of Cups can indicate a new contract or agreement. In business matters, you may meet an important associate. This is a period of emotional balance and inner well-being.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: There may be a separation of an important relationship. In some cases, the Two of Cups reversed can indicate broken trust or hurt feelings. It’s important to remember to communicate your feelings. You may feel as though you have been abandoned or rejected. Arguments and miscommunications may be affecting your relationships. It’s important to remember to pay attention to those you care about.
TaroCard.Meaning: In Tarot Reading, the Two of Cups often refers to one’s partnerships. In many cases, this is a true love card. The Two of Cups is associated to harmony and collaboration.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is a period of celebration and joy. The Three of Cups refers to marriages, engagements, births, family gatherings, reunions and religious ceremonies. Expect some good news and an abundance of good luck. Don’t be surprised if you hear news of a job promotion, a new birth, an engagement or anything else that brings joy into your life. You might meet an important business relationship through the attendance of some type of ceremony such as a wedding or a religious service.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: Be careful not to overindulge. The Three of Cups reversed can indicate too much emphasis on pleasure seeking. Something that once brought you happiness now brings new troubles. A celebration may be postponed. There could be issues of infertility or poor health. You may experience a period of sadness or dissatisfaction. A romantic relationship may encounter a period of difficulty.
TaroCard.Meaning: The three maidens in the garden correspond to the three Graces. Surrounded by bowers of blooms, they raise their cups in celebrations. It's a party time!

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is the time to turn inward and truly explore your feelings. You may be going through a period of apathy or confusion. If you have been uncertain as to which direction you need to take, this would be the time to contemplate on what truly makes you happy. In some cases, the Four of Cups can indicate the need to explore your options. You may be confronted with a new situation that you are unsure about. In love Tarot, the Four of Cups sometimes indicates that there are mixed feelings about one’s relationship.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: Now is the time to get into action. Things are starting to look up. You may be presented with an exciting opportunity. There is a new found sense of motivation and willingness to take some initiative. You may be invited to new social events or suddenly feel as though you want to engage with others. A period of isolation is ending. In Love Tarot, there may be a revival in your relationship. You may feel more committed to your partner and there is a new willingness to work things out.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Four of Cups signifies feelings of apathy and indifference. It often refers to the need to turn inward.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Five of Cups can refer to feelings of loss, disappointment and remorse. It often indicates that there is grief that you have not yet completely processed. In some cases, the Five of Cups can indicate an inability to move on from your past. The Five of Cups urges you to move beyond your former sufferings. It is a warning that a negative outlook about the future is preventing you from moving forward. This is the time to let go of regrets. In love tarot, the Five of Cups can indicate a separation or the need to let go of a relationship that may not be working for you.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: An emotionally painful period is now over. You are on the road of recovery and healing. This is a period in which you must find self-acceptance. You may need to finally come to terms with the fact that a relationship is over. In some cases, a reversed Five of Cups can indicate an over-attachment to one’s past. You cannot move forward until you are willing to let go of old hurts and wounds. Be careful that you are not projecting your past experiences into your present situation.
TaroCard.Meaning: Although two of the cups are filled, the figure wearing the "cloak of mourning" sees only what has spilled. You feel remorse over a severed relationship or unfulfilled dream.

TaroCard.DirectReading: This is a period of reminiscence, childhood memories, and the fond sentiments of your past. You may rediscover an old relationship. A lover from your past may suddenly reappear. Relationships may need to become more playful and innocent. Allow yourself to be vulnerable with your partner. In some cases, The Six of Cups denotes a resurgence of opportunities that were once missed. This may be a time of emotional renewal. Old acquaintances may offer you new opportunities. Your past efforts will prove to be successful.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: It is important to uncover the memories of your past, but do not get stuck there. Your ideas and beliefs that were established in the past may be blocking your personal development. It would be wise to use your past as a guide for your future. The Six of Cups reversed can indicate the need to live in the moment. You may need to break from past obligations that have been holding you back.
TaroCard.Meaning: In a peaceful country scene, children frolic among cups of flowers. People emerge from your past; you feel nostalgia for days gone by. You long for a lost love.

TaroCard.DirectReading: Numerous opportunities present themselves, yet you are unsure as to which direction you should take. The best approach would be to thoroughly explore all your options before you take any action. Initial appearances may be misleading. You may be unrealistic about a certain goal you wish to achieve. In some cases, the Seven of Cups indicates that you are spending too much time day dreaming and are not taking the necessary actions to achieve your goals. In Love tarot, there may be some confusion about your partner or a love interest.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: It’s time to get into action. Your determination and tenacity will pay off. You are now able to see things as they really are. If you get clear about your goals, they can be easily achieved. Confusion has been replaced with clarity and you can now pursue a new direction. Focus on what is essential and act decisively. The more realistic you are, the better the chances are for a successful outcome. If your efforts have failed in the past, now is the time to take what you have learned and try again.
TaroCard.Meaning: Conjured by a wizard, fantastic creations emerge from the cups. The Seven of Cups encourages you to explore all your options before taking any action. It’s important to center yourself and clear your mind.

TaroCard.DirectReading: Now may be the time to move on or let go of a situation. You need to leave the past behind you. Free yourself and start something new. You may have to deal with the relationships that are no longer working for you. This may be a time where you need to explore your own independence. In some cases, the Eight of Cups can indicate a change in residence or travel. In love tarot, the Eight of Cups can refer to a separation or hurt feelings. One partner may let the other down.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may be struggling with letting go of a relationship. The reversed Eight of Cups can indicate co-dependency or the fear of being alone. There is too much emphasis on the past. It’s time to look towards your future. It’s important get in touch with your inner voice and inner truth. You may need more clarity about a specific situation. Your fears may be preventing you from seeing things as they really are.
TaroCard.Meaning: A pilgrim flees into the night under the watchful gaze of the moon. In a Tarot reading, the Eight of Cups represents leaving the past behind and moving forward. Although this may be a painful process, it is a necessary one.

TaroCard.DirectReading: Your wishes will come true. The Nine of Cups often refers to happiness, well-being, financial comfort, pleasure and personal fulfillment. This is a period of personal satisfaction and gratification. Important projects are completed with successful outcomes. You may receive a marriage proposal or land the perfect job. If you are single, you just may meet the perfect partner. In business matters, there is growth and expansion. Remember to have some fun and enjoy the labors of your hard work.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: Your expectations may be unrealistic. You may be overindulging in things that are not good for you. There may be too much of an emphasis on material gain and possessions. In financial matters, there could be a loss or setback. In love Tarot, self-centered behavior is causing conflict within the relationship. One partner may not be considering the feelings of others.
TaroCard.Meaning: Surrounded by golden cups, a man beams happily. The peacock feather in his hat denotes good luck. This "Wish Card" promises that a wish, probably of a material nature, will be granted to the Questioner.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Ten of Cups is the card of prosperity and contentment. This is a period where there will be harmony and unity within your relationships. You may attend social events or family gatherings. In love Tarot, the Ten of Cups can denote a marriage, birth or pregnancy. Business endeavors will thrive and your undertakings will be met with success. You may get a salary increase or promotion. There will be a sense of well-being in all areas of your life. When the Ten of Cups appears in a Tarot reading, one can expect all things to improve.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: It’s important to remember to appreciate the things that you have and not take those that you care about for granted. On an emotional level, the Ten of Cups reversed can indicate feelings of sadness or loss. There may be some disturbances in your home environment. There may be family quarrels or disagreements. In love Tarot, there may be conflicts that come up in a significant relationship. The Ten of Cups reversed urges you to share your feelings about the things you do appreciate about your partner.
TaroCard.Meaning: A happy family beholds the rainbow in a scene of great joy. This card signifies fulfillment, happiness, and domestic harmony.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Page of Cups is an artist. He lives in the realm of his imagination and is highly intuitive. He is often the messenger of births and pregnancies. When he appears in a Tarot reading, it usually is an indicator that something new will emerge in your life. This is a great time for creative endeavors. You may receive and important message. A current relationship may develop towards a deeper level of intimacy. In love Tarot, the Page of Cups can indicate a new romantic relationship.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may be hesitating in taking an important risk. In some circumstances, a reversed Page of Cups can refer to not living up to your potential. Your insecurities are prohibiting you from growing. Remember to remain open to new opportunities, particularly to those that relate to relationships. In love Tarot, the Page of Cups reversed can refer to a fear of rejection or an unwillingness to get vulnerable. You may be ignoring your feelings.
TaroCard.Meaning: A fish emerges from the cup, to the Page's surprise. The Page is sensitive, thoughtful, helpful, and loyal.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Knight of Cups loves a challenge and appreciates anything that tests his mind. He is sensitive and emotional. He is extremely romantic and falls in love easily. His appearance in a Tarot reading urges you to follow your heart. There may be a significant situation that concerns your emotions or your relationships. You may meet a new love interest. In some cases, the Knight of Cups can indicate a new offer or business opportunity. Your idealism and imagination set you apart from others.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: The reversed Knight of Cups can be a warning that you are being overly influenced by others. Be careful of those who offer you something that seems like it is too good to be true. It would be wise to explore new relationships before you commit to them. In business matters, make sure you thoroughly review contracts and agreements. You may need to stand your ground or be firm in your negotiations. In Love Tarot, a reversed Knight of Cups can indicate a partner that has a fear of commitment or intimacy. He or she may be irresponsible or lack direction.
TaroCard.Meaning: Astride a white steed, this knight gazes upon a chalice - the Holy Grail? - as the road winds before him. This attractive and persuasive individual is on a quest, perhaps romantic or spiritual.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Queen of Cups is intuitive by nature. She tends to be sensitive to those around her. Her ability to connect to others enables her to have an abundance of close relationships. When she appears in a Tarot reading, there may be a need to tune into your emotions and feelings. There may be a situation in which you need to let go of your intellect and listen to your heart. It’s also important to become aware of your dreams and intuition. Creative endeavors can give you great emotional satisfaction at this time. There may be others that come to you for emotional support.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: Your emotions may be influencing your perspectives. It’s important to remember to not overlook the negative behaviors of others. You also need to be careful with whom you go to for advice. A reversed Queen of Cups can indicate a woman who cannot keep secrets. In Love Tarot, a reversed Queen of Cups can indicate betrayal or a relationship that lacks emotional satisfaction. There could also be a tendency towards having too high of expectations from your partner.
TaroCard.Meaning: This queen drinks deeply from the cup of life. Her emotions and sexuality are intense; she relies on intuition before intellect.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The King of Cups reflects our initiative and desire to get things done. He is incredibly creative and tends examine things from a unique perspective. This is the time to channel your creative energies into concrete actions. Set your goals as high as you can expect for successful results. This will be a period of emotional balance and stability. In a Tarot reading, the King of Cups can indicate a compassionate friend or wise advisor. You may get recognized for your leadership abilities. In love Tarot, the King of Cups represents a mature, responsible and compassionate man.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: You may have issues with a controlling or manipulative person. It’s important to remain cautious of the advice you are given. There could be deception or foul play. This is also a time to manage your emotions. You may be confronted with a situation that can trigger your emotions. It would be wise to take some time to evaluate your feelings. Acting impulsively can cause some regret. In love Tarot, a reversed King of Cups can indicate a partner that is not authentic or who tends to be out only for himself.
TaroCard.Meaning: Like Neptune, the King of Cups reigns over the sea. His authority calms turbulent waters. He is creative and compassionate - often a doctor or counselor.

TaroCard.DirectReading: Here, you are facing adversity. You must remain strong and be true to your principles. The utilization of your mind, logic, and determination will help you confront your current challenges. The most important thing to remember is to believe in your own abilities. This is the time to rise to the occasion. Your confidence and strength of will can help you overcome your fears. The energy of the Ace of Swords initiates the time for new intellectual endeavors. In some cases, the Ace of Swords can indicate potential health issues.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In the reversed position, the Ace of Swords suggests that you could be using too much force. You may be using your power as a means to intimidate people. Be careful not to use your strength in a negative way or your forceful behavior may cause you to burn important bridges. In love Tarot, this card suggests that you might be in such a relationship yourself; where you are at risk of not being heard, are fearful, or feel confined by an overbearing partner. Finally if your card pertains to health, the Ace of Swords reversed may indicate protracted problems or a very long recovery.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Aces of Swords have significant meaning. They, like the major arcana, often represent the onset of a new life cycle. They refer to new beginnings and important crossroads. They convey a raw power, propelling us forward into a new area of personal growth.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Two of Swords indicates that you are at an impasse. You may be feeling overwhelmed or are lacking in clarity. If you are falsely relying on your intellect, you may be overlooking your true feelings. Choosing to ignore you personal truths may cause you further troubles. By releasing your thoughts and emotions you can have faith in the spiritual forces to guide you. Clarity and direction can often be revealed through resolution of inner conflict.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the Two of Swords suggests that your emotions have been released and tensions have been dispelled. With this new clarity, indecisiveness disappears and decisions can now be made. This may indicate a time to leap into action. However, there may still be a period of delay for things to develop. Patience is required. A reversed Two of Swords reminds you that your own fears can halt your personal growth.
TaroCard.Meaning: The blindfold and crossed swords denote a situation that is delicately balanced. Diplomacy is required, but agreement can be reached. Relations will warm up, but it will take time.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Three of Swords indicates there will be a major separation or loss from a loved one. This could be a period of deep upheaval both spiritually and emotionally. You have a need for cleansing and a catharsis of your emotions. This action is necessary in order for you to have a shift in your perspective. The Three of Swords also represents the fear of or actual abandonment. Experiencing the grief is crucial to healing.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: The end of your pain is in sight. By processing your feelings of loss, you realize your inner strength and are ready for a new life stage. In love Tarot, the reversed Three of Swords can be associated with old wounds or trauma. It’s important to not project these experiences into your relationships. If you are not careful, this can inhibit growth for your current relationship. You must be willing to work through the issues of your past in order to move forward
TaroCard.Meaning: Three swords in the heart warn of heartbreak, adultery, and infidelity. You need to communicate with a loved one. The Three of Swords is the card of grief and sorrow, and unfortunately, the three of swords informs us that this cannot be avoided. One must move through the process of letting go.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Four of Swords is a card of respite. Often the Four of Swords suggests that you have finally overcome a major obstacle. It is now time for you to recover and heal. Do not be concerned about inactivity; regroup, meditate and contemplate. A vacation may be in sight, or this may be a great time to plan one. Health-wise, the Four of Swords indicates recovery.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: This is the time to get back into action. You need to be present in your life. It is time to resume your daily activities again. However, in some cases, you or someone close to you may need to examine your behaviors. There is a risk of becoming too isolated. You may face rejection or loss of a job. In some cases, a Four of Swords can indicate health issues that can hamper your energy levels.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Four of Swords is a card of inaction. It typically indicates the need to take some time to relax and recharge.

TaroCard.DirectReading: Someone that you know may be having a negative effect on you by challenging you at work or within your home. Be cautious of this competition and become aware of the negative impact that an ego battle can bring. Do not lose yourself in manipulation or selfishness. With hostility in the air it is important to examine the relationships that you are in. There may be betrayal or deceit. In love Tarot, your relationships may be complicated and argumentative. Someone’s feelings may get hurt.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the Five of Swords indicates that dishonesty and intimidation are causing your current situation to be unsuccessful. By possible bullying, you are feeling degraded and humiliated. These feelings stem from feeling victimized. This is a good time to explore this and take responsibility for your own actions or lack of self-esteem. On a positive note, the reversed Five of Swords can indicate that a troublesome battle will soon be over. Competition and unwarranted gossip will soon cease to be a problem.
TaroCard.Meaning: Two unarmed figures take flight. Signifies a withdrawal after conflict, or a victory without peace. It's a bad time to make enemies.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The stress is over and you are entering a period of tranquility where you can expect advantageous changes. You can now let yourself go with the flow. The Six of Swords may also indicate travel for you or a visitor from far away. This is the time to explore your relationships. You may need to ask yourself how your past is affecting them. This is an excellent time to leave an unhealthy relationship. Break from old behaviors and negative thinking. It's time to move forward.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: The reversed Six of Swords indicates a difficulty in moving beyond conflict and tension. Things have come to a standstill and progress has been delayed. Travel plans may be halted or delayed. Perhaps you are feeling trapped and are unable to see a way out of your difficulties. You need to be more conscious of your circumstances and be prepared to work harder towards personal growth.
TaroCard.Meaning: A strong man transports swords in a boat. Relief will come after a struggle. You may be taking a sea voyage.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Seven of Swords holds several messages of caution. In reaching your goals people may anticipate your actions, so do the unpredictable. In business take care to scrutinize those you are involved with as theft, lawsuits or other problems are possible. Be careful of self-defeating actions and those who may take advantage of others. The Seven of Swords can indicate a need to have a readiness to cut ties with negative relationships and to move forward in your life.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: With the Seven of Swords in a reversed position, you can expect an apology coming your way. Something taken from you will be returned. You may receive constructive criticism; be open to advice and suggestions. Keep sight of your goals with a steady awareness so you don’t miss opportunities. The reversed Seven of Swords also warns against laziness and indecision. Hard work and self-management will be rewarded with acknowledgment and success.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Seven of Swords is a card of caution. This is the time to carefully observe your surroundings.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Eight of Swords represents anxiety, fear and restrictions that are, typically, self-imposed. You might feel unable to work through emotional blocks or feel trapped in your current situation. The Eight of Swords reminds us that we have the capacity to free ourselves at any time we choose. Fear of the unknown is stopping your ability to move forward. Affirm your ability by trying something new. In love Tarot, you may feel confined or desire more personal freedom.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: A reversed Eight of Swords indicates that you will experience an emotional release of some kind. Denial, anxiety and stress will be lifted. You can now perceive your situation with clarity. This is a time of personal empowerment. You can assertively walk through your fears. As negative thinking is replaced with positive, new doors will open. You are now free to do what you choose.
TaroCard.Meaning: A blindfolded and bound figure is surrounded by danger. This difficult situation cannot be ignored. If bad news comes, face it squarely, even if there is nothing you can do.

TaroCard.DirectReading: Drawing the Nine of Swords indicates deep emotional issues, many times showing themselves in nightmares. Worry and anxiety are pervasive, ruling your thoughts. It’s important to realize that most of your fears, doubts and feelings of guilt are of your own making. You may feel periods of grief, depression, discouragement or sadness. In your highly emotional state, the criticism you receive from others can create anguish for you. However, the Nine of Swords suggests that your experiences are really not as bad as you imagine.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: A reversed Nine of Swords is a card of encouragement. While you may still feel sad, the depression and associated anxiety are lifting. There is a light at the end of the tunnel and a new feeling of hope. Help is on the way. The negative aspect of a reversed Nine of Swords is the continuation of worry and despair. This may be a period in which counseling could benefit you.
TaroCard.Meaning: In many cases, the Nine of Swords serves as a reminder that your anxieties are not founded in truth. Much of your despair is of your own making.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Ten of Swords appears terrifying, but it can have an optimistic perspective. Symbolized as the end of a cycle, your life can take a new direction by letting go of the past and moving forward. Traditionally, the Ten of Swords suggest that, on some level, you have bottomed out. Regardless of the feelings of loss, you must let go of situations in which there can be no resolution. There may be a concern over legal issues or health complications.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: With the Ten of Swords in a reversed position, you can now expect a period of recovery. You have survived and your cycle of chaos, sadness and grief is coming to an end. Seek and accept support from others. This is also a great time to connect to your own spirituality. In some cases, the Ten of Swords can signify final endings. There may be a death that occurred in your past, but you have not fully dealt with your grief. This is the time to allow yourself to feel the emotions you previously were not ready to process.
TaroCard.Meaning: This is a card of perfect desolation. Major changes are on the way, and resistance is futile. A path clears itself, giving way to something new.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Page of Swords may indicate that you may find yourself in a situation where quick observation and analysis are needed. You may find yourself challenged by abrasive forms of communication. Navigate through your current situations by utilizing your intellect and objectivity. The Page of Swords is also the messenger of important news. Rely on rational thinking and proceed with caution, particularly with important negotiations. A young person’s behavior can also be a concern to you.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: A reversed Page of Swords suggests a time of unpredictability. You may face miscommunications, broken promises, or hurt feelings. Carefully examine important paperwork. The reversed Paige of Swords can indicate scandal or even blackmail. A child in your life may be rebellious or disruptive. Be certain to set clear boundaries
TaroCard.Meaning: This perceptive young person is ready for action. The card signifies quick thinking. Can also indicate spying or trouble with the police.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The Knight of Swords calls for immediate action. You may find yourself in a conflicting situation that requires confidence and fearlessness. Trust that this situation will go as quickly as it came. You are in an active time requiring you to stand up for your beliefs. Listen to your head and seek advice in legal matters. A strong, yet impetuous young man may come into your life.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the Knight of Swords may indicate the departure of someone in your life, particularly a male. Do not undertake a new project and expect delays in your current plans. Your endeavors may be influenced by others, so remain diplomatic. You may be trying to control a situation through force. Be wary of your intentions. Selfish behavior may cause you problems in your relationships.
TaroCard.Meaning: The Knight charges bravely into battle. He's a skilled warrior who rushes into situations without weighing the consequences. His charming nature gets him out of scrapes.

TaroCard.DirectReading: In a tarot reading, the Queen of Swords suggests that this may be a period where you must find your own independence and autonomy. Your determination and strength of character can lead you. You may find yourself in a situation that requires you to be assertive and expressive. Your analytical mind is attractive to others, particularly to those involved in your work environment. This may be a period where your career takes center stage. The Queen of Swords encourages you to try something new. She can also symbolize a woman who has suffered, but remains courageous and strong.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the Queen of Swords is a woman influenced by her own vindictiveness. She is prone to undermining you. Be careful that your past has not left you feeling resentful and slighted. Reconnect with your feelings and do not allow yourself to be manipulated by force or intimidation. The Queen of Swords warns against too much emphasis on intellect. Remain balanced, fair and non-judgmental.
TaroCard.Meaning: The sword in the Queen's hand represents her quick wits - and her sharp tongue. The widow, like other woman in difficulty, continues bravely despite loss. Her keen intelligence and cool, logical approach make her appear aloof.

TaroCard.DirectReading: The King of Swords is a card of truth, balance and impartial judgment. This is the time to use your skills of negotiation, objectivity and acute observation. Your independent nature will provide you with new leadership opportunities. Be original and use your intellect to think outside of the box. This may also be a good time to seek advice from an expert. Do not, however, neglect your emotions or you may be at risk of alienating yourself from others.
TaroCard.ReverseReading: In a reversed position, the King of Swords can indicate that you have experienced some form of injustice. Use your analytical thinking to contest such issues. There may be control and domination issues. In legal affairs, the King of Swords reversed indicates a poor outcome. Work hard not to use your power to manipulate or take advantage of others.
